Subject: AWS co-op fund and listing fee model — initial ask

Sooj, Laura —

Following up from last week's partner sync: AWS has sent an updated co-op and listing fee framework that would impact our listing economics starting Q4. Attached is the spreadsheet they shared (aws_fee_schedule_q2.xlsx). High level: they want a 5% listing fee plus an optional co-op fund where they take 2% and credit it back as marketing funds if we meet specific quarterly milestones.

Questions I have for finance/legal before I engage Sarah formally:
- Do we accept the co-op-as-credit structure or insist on a direct rebate?
- If we accept, need to confirm whether the credit is earmarked (marketing-only) or can be used against fees.
- What guardrails should we ask for in the contract (cap on deductions, clawback / audit language)?

Can you review (esp. the milestone language on tab "MarketingCredits") and let me know if we should push for a reduced % or additional protections?

Thanks,

Sarah — looping you in. Karthik pulled the schedule and asked a couple of clarifying questions about co-op vs rebate structure (see attached overview). High level asks from our side: we need the co-op to be a true marketing credit (not an automatic deduction from our payout) and we need visibility into how milestones are measured and audited.

Specific asks:
- Can AWS confirm whether the 2% co-op will be invoiced and then issued as a credit (preferred), or applied as a pre-deduction on payouts?
- If it is a marketing credit, can it be used for any AWS marketing program (not restricted to marketplace-only activities)?
- Can we get an explicit cap on retroactive clawbacks (e.g., 90-day limit) and a right to dispute measurement reports?

I've attached a short company overview to help your partnerships team (redwood_corp_overview.pdf). Appreciate any clarity; if it helps we can do a quick 30-min sync next week.

Best,

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear notes and the overview PDF. Quick answers below and attaching the formal coop terms (aws_coop_terms_v2.pdf).

1) Mechanics: the co-op is typically invoiced and then applied as a marketing credit once milestones are verified. We do not auto-deduct co-op from payouts without prior notice; that said, marketplace listing fees (the 5%) are deducted at settlement.
2) Use of funds: credits are eligible for AWS marketing programs, including marketplace campaigns and sponsored content. We can make exceptions for partner-specific programs on a case-by-case basis — we should outline the use-cases during the close.
3) Clawback/audit: standard is a 120-day audit window. We're open to a 90-day limit if you provide a reporting cadence that supports it. There is a dispute resolution process in the partner contract — happy to share the standard flow.

Next steps:
- I can escalate this to our Partner Programs team and request explicit language that makes credits usable beyond marketplace campaigns.
- If Redwood provides a one-page list of desired contract changes, I can fast-track review.

Happy to hop on a call early next week to align.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Sr. Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
Amazon.com, Inc.

Thanks for the thread — Sarah, appreciated.

From a finance/procurement perspective:
- We should accept the invoice-then-credit approach (minimizes surprise deductions) but require the 90-day audit window and explicit dispute SLA as a condition.
- Request that credits be usable for a broader set of AWS marketing programs by default; if they push back we can accept case-by-case exceptions with a written escalation path.
- Ask for a cap on retroactive deductions beyond 3 months unless there is evidence of fraud.

Operational asks:
- Procurement needs the final partner language (DocuSign-ready) and a list of how credits will be measured (events, conversion metrics).
- Please include a sample reporting extract — we'll need it for our monthly reconciliation.

If Sarah can get Partner Programs to provide the one-pager with the proposed language, procurement can sign off and get this into the renewal pipeline.

Laura Bennett
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
